name: Melt De-pivot
description: Keeps the chosen fixed fields and turns every other field into records: one record per input record and field, with the field's name and its value. Values of different types become text.
introductoryText:
Turns a wide table into a long one. Choose the fields to keep as they are (**Fixed fields**, such as an ID or name); every other field is de-pivoted: each input record becomes one output record per de-pivoted field, holding the fixed fields, the de-pivoted field's **name** and its **value**.

For example, a table with Store, Jan, Feb and Mar becomes Store, Field, Value, with three records per store.

**How to set it up**

- **Fixed fields**: the fields to keep on every output record. Leave empty to de-pivot every field.
- **Name field** and **Value field**: names for the two new fields (default Field and Value). They must differ from each other and from the fixed fields.
- **Leave out empty values**: tick to skip records whose value is empty.

Each input record's values come out together, in the order of the fields. If the de-pivoted fields are of one type (all numbers, all dates, all text), the value field has that type; if they are of different types, every value is turned into text (whole numbers without decimals, dates as yyyy-mm-dd), and the block's message says so.

Omniscope's core De-pivot block does the same job with rule-based field selection and needs no Python; this block is a script you can adapt.
